title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Oil jumped ~2% (Brent ~$89.46, WTI ~$84.60) after the US struck Iranian rocket launchers near Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz, reigniting Middle East escalation fears
Markets: US stock futures slipped Monday (Dow -0.3%, S&P -0.4%, Nasdaq -0.4%) on the Iran news; Asia-Pacific markets fell broadly (Nikkei, Kospi, Hang Seng, CSI 300 all down)
Markets: Wall Street is still closing out a strong August — S&P +3%, Nasdaq +4% (first monthly gains since May), Dow's 5th straight monthly advance
Companies: Shein priced its Hong Kong IPO at the midpoint (HK$48.56/share), raising ~$1.7B at a ~$26.5B valuation — about 70% below its 2022 peak; shares begin trading Sept. 1
Macro/Policy: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh struck a hawkish tone at Jackson Hole, saying he wants underlying inflation clearly heading lower; the dollar firmed on rate-hike bets
Macro/Policy: Core PCE inflation held at a sticky 3.3% y/y in July as consumer spending stalled; next FOMC decision is Sept. 15-16 with only ~1-in-3 odds of a move currently priced in
